title: Overcoming the Hong-Ou-Mandel interference limitation for the second photon from a two-photon cascade
authors: Raphael Joos, Michal Vyvlecka, Tim Strobel, Benjamin Breiholz, Furkan Aglarci, Ponraj Vijayan, Hans-Georg Babin, Arne Ludwig, Michael Jetter, Simone L. Portalupi, Peter Michler
abstract: Quantum emitters such as semiconductor quantum dots can provide entangled photon pairs emitting from a system of cascaded states. However, the resulting temporal correlation between the two photons from the three-level ladder system has been shown to set a limit on the achievable two-photon interference. In this work, we show that such limitation, for photons emitted by the second transition, is only due to reduced temporal overlap at the interference beam splitter. We investigate this theoretically and experimentally by determining time-resolved four-photon coincidences between two successively emitted photon pairs. Post-emission synchronization shows the recovery of maximum interference visibility; in prospective quantum networks this could be achieved via deterministic quantum memories.
summary: This work investigates how to overcome the inherent limitation on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference visibility when using cascaded emission from quantum dots. Theoretically and experimentally, the authors demonstrate that the visibility loss is due to temporal mismatch at the beam splitter, not the emission process itself. By implementing post-emission synchronization, they show that near-unity interference visibility can be recovered, advancing the feasibility of solid-state quantum sources for quantum networking.
main_problem: The paper addresses the limitation on Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference visibility for the second photon emitted during a two-photon cascade process from quantum emitters.
main_result: The limitation is shown to stem from reduced temporal overlap at the interference beam splitter, not the cascade process itself, and maximum visibility can be recovered via post-emission synchronization.
method: The study combines theoretical derivation of time-resolved four-photon coincidences with experimental measurements using time-resolved coincidence counting.
model_or_system: The system uses semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) exhibiting an XX-X cascade, modeled as a three-level ladder system, to generate entangled photon pairs.
key_observables: Time-resolved four-photon coincidence probability density function $p_{\parallel/\perp}^{(4)}(	au_E, 	au_L)$ and the average HOM visibility $V_{	ext{avg}}^{	ext{HOM,L}}$.
important_parameters: Time delays ($	au_E, 	au_L$), input delays ($\delta t_0$), and spectral broadening parameter ($\sigma$).
main_assumptions: The late photon interference visibility is assumed to be determined solely by the temporal overlap at the beam splitter.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy level structure and experimental setup, showing calculated time-resolved HOM visibility and measured probability density functions for different input delays.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical model and the limitation, derives the four-photon correlation function, and then presents experimental measurements using time-resolved coincidence detection to confirm the dependence on temporal overlap.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, experimentally verifiable mechanism for enhancing quantum interference visibility in solid-state sources, which is crucial for building scalable quantum networks.
